misconceptions.believed: That Functional for a fight could be computed by pooling the fight's total ops against the reference's total ops, the way a level compares one submission to one reference. Summing seemed obviously right because ops accumulate.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Running the suite before writing a test for it, and reading the output rather than the exit status. A fight that stopped on step one printed functional 100.0 beside accuracy 44.4.
misconceptions.corrected_to: Functional is computed per step and averaged, and a step that passed nothing scores zero rather than the ratio of the work it skipped. A fight that stops early never defines the later functions, so they execute nothing; pooled against the reference that reads as doing less work, functional_score caps the ratio at 1.0, and the card congratulates a player who achieved almost nothing. Per-step also stops one frugal step subsidising a wasteful one.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: This is M1's shape for the fifth recorded time: free points on an axis that is not measuring anything. Every instance so far was found by looking at what a bad run printed, never by the test suite -- because a test written by whoever wrote the bug asserts the same wrong thing. Test a scoring system with a bad solution, and read the output.

misconceptions.believed: That Weights.without_speed() fully drops the Speed axis. The weight becomes 0, so the axis cannot affect the total, so the axis is dropped.
misconceptions.revealed_by: A test asserting score.speed == 0.0 for a practice fight, which got 100.0. The value was still computed against a clock that had started moments earlier; only its contribution was suppressed.
misconceptions.corrected_to: score_fight zeroes Speed when the axis carries no weight. N5 says an axis that cannot be measured honestly must not be scored, and a ScoreBreakdown is stored and read back later -- a zero weight hides the number from the total, not from whoever quotes the record afterwards.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: score_submission has the same property today: a practice-mode level run banks a computed speed from a clock that started when the file was read, invisible only because cmd_play prints 'not measured' instead of the gauge. Fixing it would change level scoring and previously banked records, so it was left alone deliberately and raised as Q81 rather than quietly changed.

misconceptions.believed: That the existing boss tests captured everything cmd_boss printed, since they all wrapped it in redirect_stdout.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Three new assertions failing against transcripts with the score cut out of the middle, while the gauges appeared on the real terminal during the run.
misconceptions.corrected_to: UI binds sys.stdout when it is constructed, at import time, so redirect_stdout catches the plain print calls and misses every gauge and star burst. One everything_printed() helper now swaps both, used by all four fight harnesses. Not a product bug -- in a real pipe sys.stdout is the pipe -- but the boss tests had been asserting against partial transcripts and would have kept doing so silently.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: A capture helper that misses half the output does not fail; it just narrows what the assertions can see. Assert on something you know is printed before trusting a transcript.

decisions.decision: BOSS DOWN is a mastery ending; the HP and repair mechanics are unchanged
alternatives: First repair free of its heal (floor 51)
First repair free entirely (floor 0, but flawless becomes the default outcome)
decisions.rationale: The measurement showed the heal is not the obstacle, so three of the four options were dials rather than answers. The one that reaches zero makes the rare ending common. Reached by returning with a solution that passes every step first time, which is the same shape as replaying a level for a third star.

decisions.decision: Hit points are not an input to the score
alternatives: Fold remaining HP into the total
decisions.rationale: HP already prices how wrong the code was through W6's heal curve. Scoring it again is exactly what CLAUDE.md section 4 prohibits. The pool reaches the score once, through first_try.

decisions.decision: Accuracy is pooled across cases; Functional is averaged per step
decisions.rationale: Accuracy keeps the single definition it has everywhere else -- the fraction of hidden tests passed. Functional is per step because each step has its own reference, and because pooling produced M40.

decisions.decision: The engine subtracts its own slow motion from the Speed clock
alternatives: Give the boss a longer par to absorb the animation
decisions.rationale: Counting it scores a display setting: the same fight played identically at --speed 0.1 and --speed 2.0 would earn different marks. A longer par shrinks the distortion without making it honest.

decisions.decision: An abandoned fight is still scored
alternatives: Print no card unless the fight cleared
decisions.rationale: A zero printed for a reason is information; a blank reads as an omission. The starters fail by contract, so the abandoned fight is what a first-time player actually gets -- leaving it unscored would mean the only scored fight is one nobody has had.

decisions.decision: T3 holds IN FLIGHT until W8 ships
alternatives: Land on the six criteria and record W8 as a gap in the criteria list
Land and re-scope W8 to another trajectory
decisions.rationale: The user's call on Q77. The waypoint list is treated as the real contract and the exit criteria as incomplete, which is a finding about the criteria rather than a licence to edit them (N7).

friction.description: Deciding where the 'how wrong were you before repairing' signal belongs. The heal curve measures it, the score cannot see it because a cleared fight is 100% accurate by definition, and scoring it in both places violates section 4. Justifying the resolution -- HP is the outcome, the card is the grade, printed side by side -- took longer than implementing it. The alternative is recorded as Q82 rather than discarded.

open_questions.question: Should the pane have a 'replace this function' affordance?
Is BOSS DOWN being unreachable from the starters a defect?
open_questions.answer: No. It is a mastery ending, reached by returning with a solution that passes every step first time. The floor from the starters was measured at exactly 65, and the heal is only 14 of the missing 35, so the alternatives were dials rather than answers (D158).

open_questions.question: score_submission stores a computed speed for practice runs, from a clock that started when the file was read. The UI hides it; the stored record does not. score_fight was written not to. Should the level path match, and what happens to already-banked runs?

The score cannot see how wrong the code was before it was repaired. A cleared fight is 100% accurate whether it was patched from 90% or from a guess; only HP distinguishes them. Is reporting the two side by side enough, or should the card read first-attempt accuracy?
